supersedes: evidence/310-mutant-prerebase.json - snapped before the coordinator's rebase, when the `scripts` stage did not yet contain #253's two rule-17 guards (four Invoke-Checked calls) ahead of this Issue's wiring. This file re-runs the same mutant on the rebased base and adds a negative-control experiment the prerebase file did not need, answering the coordinator's specific question: does an earlier check in the stage mask this test's failure?
question: On the rebased base (scripts stage now runs #253's four rule-17 guards before this Issue's wiring), does the `scripts` stage still redden because of THIS test's failure specifically - not because of an earlier check absorbing or otherwise masking it?

baselineDirectRun.note: Unchanged from evidence/310-mutant-prerebase.json - this test does not read anything #306 or #253 touch, so its own baseline was not re-measured. It is exercised again, in full, by the full green run in evidence/310-full-verify.json.

method: Verified clean via 'git status --short' before mutating (HEAD at 0a9446d, nothing modified). Applied the mutant, ran 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts', recorded the result, then ran a second, negative-control experiment on top - commenting out only this Issue's Invoke-Checked call while leaving the mutant in place - to isolate whether the wiring itself, not some other check, is the necessary and sufficient cause of the reddening. Restored both files with 'git checkout -- scripts/verify.ps1 scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1' between and after, re-verifying 'git status --short' was clean each time.

mutant.name: forced failure at the top of test-token-budget-report.ps1 (same mutant as evidence/310-mutant-prerebase.json)

diff.replace:
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

# MUTANT (Issue #310 evidence, reverted before commit): forced failure to
# prove the `scripts` stage of verify.ps1 reddens when this test fails.
throw "MUTANT-310: forced failure to prove the scripts stage reddens."

mutant.observedFailurePath: The mutant text ("MUTANT-310: forced failure...") appears twice in the run's output. First occurrence: scripts/test-verify-stages.ps1 (this Issue's check #5 in the stage body, after #253's four new rule-17 guards) runs its own pre-existing engine-gate proof, which spawns a real nested 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts' child process as part of a check unrelated to this Issue (proving the stage refuses a bogus -GodotPath even though its body never calls Godot). That nested child process runs the full, real scripts stage - including this Issue's Invoke-Checked call at the end of it - and dies on the same mutant, which surfaces as test-verify-stages.ps1's own check #5 failing with a confusing, seemingly-unrelated error. Second occurrence: the same mutant text embedded in that failure's propagated diagnostics. The stage therefore reddens at check #5 (verify_stages_test), not visibly at check #16 (this Issue's own call) - because check #5's nested subprocess reaches the mutant first, before the outer script's own execution gets there.
mutant.concernThisRaises: Does check #5 failing first mean the stage would redden on this mutant even without this Issue's wiring existing at all - i.e., is the observed reddening actually caused by something else, with this Issue's own Invoke-Checked call never meaningfully exercised?

negativeControlExperiment.purpose: Directly answers the concern above and the coordinator's question: is this Issue's wiring the necessary and sufficient cause of the stage reddening on this mutant, or could an earlier check (in particular #253's four new guards, or the pre-existing test-verify-stages.ps1 engine-gate check) mask/cause it independent of this Issue's own call?
negativeControlExperiment.setup: With the mutant from above still in place (throw at the top of scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1, unchanged), additionally commented out this Issue's own Invoke-Checked call in scripts/verify.ps1's `scripts` stage body - the exact four lines added by this PR - leaving every other check (including #253's four guards and the nested engine-gate check inside test-verify-stages.ps1) untouched.

diff.replace:
# NEGATIVE CONTROL (Issue #310 evidence, reverted before commit): line
            # commented out to prove the wiring itself - not some earlier check -
            # is what makes the mutant in test-token-budget-report.ps1 redden this
            # stage.
            # Invoke-Checked -FilePath "powershell" -Arguments @(
            #     "-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", $tokenBudgetReportTestScript
            # )
        }
    }

negativeControlExperiment.reasoning: With this Issue's wiring removed, nothing anywhere in the process tree calls the mutated scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1 - not directly, and not through test-verify-stages.ps1's nested subprocess either, because that nested subprocess is itself an invocation of the same committed verify.ps1 file, which (with the wiring line removed) no longer calls it. The stage runs clean in 121.7 s (all other 15 checks, no transcript scan) despite the mutant text still sitting, unreachable, inside test-token-budget-report.ps1.
negativeControlExperiment.conclusion: This is a clean negative control: mutant present + wiring present -> red (previous block); mutant present + wiring absent -> green. The only variable changed between the two runs is this Issue's own four-line Invoke-Checked call. That isolates the cause precisely: the reddening in the first run is not an artifact of #253's four new guards, nor a coincidence of test-verify-stages.ps1's pre-existing engine-gate check - it exists only because, and exactly because, this Issue wires the test in. #253's guards cannot structurally mask a later check's failure in this file's design either way: each Invoke-Checked call is a separate, blocking child-process invocation that throws immediately on nonzero exit (scripts/verify.ps1 Invoke-Checked, lines ~106-108 pre-rebase / ~139 post-rebase), so an earlier passing check simply falls through to the next statement - there is no shared state through which it could swallow a later one's exception.

restoredCommittedState: git checkout -- scripts/verify.ps1 scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1 after each experiment; 'git status --short' clean (HEAD at 0a9446d) both times.
conclusion: The scripts stage of verify.ps1 reddens (exit 1, verification_result status=error, failedStage=scripts) when scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1 fails, and the negative-control experiment shows this reddening is caused specifically by this Issue's own wiring, not masked or substituted by #253's two new rule-17 guards, #306's MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE change, or the pre-existing engine-gate check in test-verify-stages.ps1. The stage-#5-vs-check-#16 ordering artifact (mutant surfacing via a nested subprocess before the outer script's own direct call is reached) is a pre-existing property of test-verify-stages.ps1's engine-gate proof - present identically in the pre-rebase run (evidence/310-mutant-prerebase.json's 'sideEffectObserved') - not something #253 or #306 introduced.
